notes: Vanilla item ids with base price, flavor description, and structured effects from data.win. Effect entries use add_<stat> values; timed buffs include per-effect turns; uses is item use count. Grass includes herbs and mushrooms. Death Cap id=stool. Gwynnel's Elixir id=aqua_vitae. Honeycomb id=honey. Smoking Mix id=pipe_hemp. Spirit is the potion alcohol base. Items holds containers (flask). Coatings are weapon oils/pastes; on use they add fire or poison damage to weapons (coat_weapon_fire_damage / coat_weapon_poison_damage, optional coat_weapon_hits). Throwables are combat flasks: throw_fire_damage / throw_poison_damage / throw_gas effects with throw_aoe 1 (single target) or 3 (3x3); may include throw_ignite_turns, throw_poisoning, throw_coughing, throw_vision, spore_cloud_turns. Debuff throwables apply enemy status effects (vision, movement, combat penalties) via throw_* keys and named debuffs with icon sprites under Sprites/ (s_alch_db_*). Recipes: up to 4 ingredient ids (repeats allowed), enabled flag, optional debug flag (default false; when true grants the recipe scroll into player inventory on create), elixir outcome id; Elixirs may set debug true to grant that elixir into player inventory on create; ingredients_cost is sum of ingredient prices, recipe_cost adds spirit+flask when not already in ingredients, elixir_cost is target price. Bottle of Oil id=oil. Recipes may target elixirs, spirit, oil, coatings, or throwables. ingredients_cost must be between 75% and 100% of elixir_cost; recipe_cost > 100 requires spirit in ingredients; 80 < elixir_cost < 150 requires spirit and flask in ingredients.

grass.name: Agrimony
grass.description: Agrimony powders and infusions can do wonders for a weakened body.

grass.name: Bogbean
grass.description: Also known as buckbean, this plant can easily be found around swamps. It stimulates appetite and is often used in various tonics.

grass.name: Burdock
grass.description: This weed grows along roads and fences. Its roots are valued for their numerous medicinal properties.

grass.name: Burnet
grass.description: A herb used to staunch fresh wounds and keep infection at bay.

grass.name: Crimson Spleenwort
grass.description: Crimson spleenwort is used to hasten recovery and healing after complex surgical procedures. Supposedly, it grows only in soil frequently soaked with blood.

grass.name: Fleawort
grass.description: There once lived a herbalist who insisted on treating pretty much everything with fleawort, from seizures to postpartum delirium. If the rumors are true, he himself died of gangrene.

grass.name: Hemp
grass.description: Hemp stalks can be woven into cheap, sturdy ropes. Of course, that's not the only use for this plant...

grass.name: Henbane
grass.description: Henbane excites the senses, but in large amounts, it's a deadly poison. In some places, it is even added to beer... to make the drinking merrier, so to speak.

grass.name: Honey Hyssop
grass.description: With the proper dosage, honey hyssop can quickly bring anyone back to health, unless the patient has already given up on themselves.

grass.name: Hop Cone
grass.description: ####To the citizens of Brynn:##Be it known that for his short-sighted actions, which led to the deaths of several city guards, Master Giselbert has been placed on trial, and from this day forth his shop along with all his property shall fall under the authority of the Grand Magistrate.##Remis Krell#Senior Scribe

grass.name: Honeycomb
grass.description: It's both a delicious treat and a remedy.

grass.name: Horsetail
grass.description: Horsetail is well known as a powerful astringent. It shouldn't be abused, though - cattle that graze on horsetail often end up dead from poisoning.

grass.name: Lavender
grass.description: Lavender brews are helpful for fortifying the body and the soul in equal measure.

grass.name: Mindwort
grass.description: Mindwort is a potent sedative, helpful in the recovery from major shocks.

grass.name: Nettle
grass.description: For all its prickly nature, nettle leaves and stems are used both as food and in medicine.

grass.name: Poppy
grass.description: Not a single pain-relieving mixture is complete without poppy sap.

grass.name: Rhubarb
grass.description: Rhubarb stems are nutritious and aid digestion. The leaves, on the other hand, are mildly toxic and best avoided.

grass.name: Rotbloom
grass.description: The eye-watering odor of rotbloom is so reminiscent of decaying meat that it draws scavengers, flies, and other pests from great distances. Nevertheless, it's a plant of many benefits, particularly in treating consumption and lung fever.

grass.name: Silverleaf
grass.description: The marvelous healing properties of silverleaf have been documented since antiquity. To the sorrow of many, centuries of unchecked foraging have pushed it to the brink of extinction.

grass.name: Spearmint
grass.description: With no shortage of practical uses, spearmint makes a fine addition to any tincture.

grass.name: Spider Vine
grass.description: During her pilgrimage to Mount Foros, Saint Theona's procession was ambushed by bandits. By the grace of the Host, the Hieronites fought them off - after which Theona performed a miracle, healing the dying and wounded with nothing more than a single sprig of spider vine.

grass.name: Thyme
grass.description: Aromatic spices, medicinal brews, herbal oils - thyme has a place in all of them.

grass.name: Wormwood
grass.description: Bitter wormwood tinctures are used by Aldorian peasants to treat digestive problems and parasite infections.

grass.name: Acorn
grass.description: During more peaceful times, acorns would be fed to pigs. These days, destitute villagers prefer to hog them all for themselves.

grass.name: Azurecap
grass.description: Glows faintly in the dark - it's said azurecaps do so by capturing and retaining moonlight.

grass.name: Death Cap
grass.description: It has claimed the lives of many careless foragers.

grass.name: Fly Agaric
grass.description: Not as deceptive as a death cap, it's easily recognizable by its bright colors.

grass.name: Marble Truffle
grass.description: The right majordomo would gladly line your pockets with gold in exchange for a basket of fresh truffles.

grass.name: Morel
grass.description: A peculiarly shaped mushroom with a distinctive sponge-like cap.

grass.name: Pale Puffball
grass.description: The pale puffball is highly toxic - some accounts tell of a hired assassin fulfilling a contract by generously dispersing its spores throughout the victim's bedroom.

grass.name: Pinecap
grass.description: Pinecaps are distant relatives of penny buns. Herbalists insist that when consumed raw, they can absorb poisons and make you feel more energetic.

fruits.name: Apple
fruits.description: An apple a day keeps the physician away.

fruits.name: Barberry
fruits.description: Few eat barberries for their taste - they're mostly consumed to treat a variety of ailments.

fruits.name: Bilberry
fruits.description: Local herbalists regard bilberries as a trusted remedy for stomachaches.

fruits.name: Blueberry
fruits.description: Sweet, with a touch of pleasant sourness. Simply delicious.

fruits.name: Dragon Fruit
fruits.description: It's hard to believe this weird fruit could come from our world. The taste is nothing short of amazing.

fruits.name: Elven Citrus
fruits.description: Hideously sour but very healthy. The nobles cringe but keep eating them.

fruits.name: Fig
fruits.description: A fruit frequently peddled by eastern merchants, tempting buyers with promises of elven longevity.

fruits.name: Gooseberry
fruits.description: It's tart enough to sour one's mood.

fruits.name: Lingonberry
fruits.description: Juicy and sugary. Goes into herbal brews, remedies, and jams.

fruits.name: Peach
fruits.description: The peach came to Aldor from the East in ancient times: back then, it was known as a "royal fruit".

fruits.name: Pear
fruits.description: The Faceless are the Palace Guard of the Great Jacinth and are considered the best warriors in all the Elven Kingdoms. Among other feats, they distinguished themselves on the frontlines of the Radiant Wars by repelling the advance of King Etbert's army.

fruits.name: Raspberry
fruits.description: So juicy it almost begs to be devoured by the handful.

vegetables.name: Beet
vegetables.description: Filling and mellow in flavor, beets are a staple of peasant cooking.

vegetables.name: Cabbage
vegetables.description: Cabbage makes up nearly half the diet of an average peasant: it's eaten raw, boiled, stewed, pickled...

vegetables.name: Carrot
vegetables.description: An excellent garnish... once you wash the dirt off.

vegetables.name: Garlic
vegetables.description: Some say its smell drives away evil spirits. In reality, it drives away pretty much everyone.

vegetables.name: Ginger Root
vegetables.description: An elven plant with a tart taste and fragrant aroma. Reputedly, it helps with hangovers and other similar ailments.

vegetables.name: Leek
vegetables.description: Fresh, green, and crisp. It'll go perfectly with most dishes.

vegetables.name: Lentils
vegetables.description: Lentils are nourishing and simple to prepare - during years of poor harvest, they save entire villages from starvation.

vegetables.name: Onion
vegetables.description: Has layers and is more than it appears.

vegetables.name: Potato
vegetables.description: You can eat it raw. But why would you?

vegetables.name: Seaweed
vegetables.description: Seaweed has been dried and eaten in Aldor since time immemorial, albeit by now its use in dishes has largely gone out of favor.

vegetables.name: Tomato
vegetables.description: Some madmen claim it to be a berry.

vegetables.name: White Radish
vegetables.description: While it was brought from the Jacinth Kingdoms fairly recently, it has already managed to take root.

stones.name: Agate
stones.description: Pliable and easy to work with, agate is an excellent material for ornaments and figurines.

stones.name: Handful of Amber
stones.description: It must have come from the shores of distant Skadia. Some of the pieces contain peculiar, long-extinct insects.

stones.name: Aquamarine
stones.description: Many believe aquamarine to be a powerful magical ward and are willing to pay good money for it.

stones.name: Diamond
stones.description: Aldwynn jewelers are the finest in all the realm. Diamonds cut by their hands adorn even the tiaras of the Great Jacinth's viziers.

stones.name: Emerald
stones.description: A rare gemstone worthy of kings - any jeweler would be glad to have it.

stones.name: Jade
stones.description: Everyone in the Jacinth Kingdoms knows that jade cures diseases and grants longevity - hence the reverence it commands there.

stones.name: Moonstone
stones.description: It shimmers like a glint of moonlight.

stones.name: Morion
stones.description: The ominous appearance of morions makes them the favorite stone of warlocks and everyone who delves into the occult and other things otherworldly.

stones.name: Ruby
stones.description: This gem is worth a fortune, valued by enchanters for its unique magical properties.

stones.name: Sapphire
stones.description: Sapphires' receptiveness to magic has long drawn the attention of sorcerers. There's a whole heap of scholarly works on the subject gathering dust in the Academy archives.

stones.name: Sea Pearls
stones.description: Perfectly round and smooth. The chill of the southern seas is still preserved within them.

stones.name: Topaz
stones.description: Topaz is a well-known good luck charm that is mostly used in inexpensive jewelry.

stones.name: Turquoise
stones.description: Much of the turquoise is mined in the mountains of Jibey, from where it reaches Aldor through the trade routes of the House of the Azure Thread.

ore.name: Charcoal Chunk
ore.description: The heart of any working forge or smithy.

ore.name: Copper Nugget
ore.description: Refined copper finds ample use in many areas: household goods, modest jewelry, smelting alloys...

ore.name: Gold Nugget
ore.description: A chunk of gold‑bearing ore from one of the Aldorian mines.

ore.name: Iron Ingot
ore.description: An ingot of solid iron that will be readily purchased by any blacksmith.

ore.name: Iron Nugget
ore.description: The flesh and blood of civilization.

ore.name: Silver Nugget
ore.description: Doesn't contain a whole lot of silver, so you won't get much from selling it.

medicine.name: Antidote Syringe
medicine.description: This ingenious contraption revolutionized the treatment of poisonings. The terrible vertigo that follows is hardly the greatest price to pay for survival.

medicine.name: Antitoxin

medicine.name: Bandage
medicine.description: Might keep you from bleeding out.

medicine.name: Bloodletting Lancet
medicine.description: Many physicians firmly believe that occasional, well-placed incisions can draw out tainted blood, thus staving off diseases.

medicine.name: Ether Inhaler
medicine.description: The invention of one of the royal physicians: the fumes within this bizarre vessel are poisonous, but they ease pain and clear the mind.

medicine.name: Healing Salve
medicine.description: Originally, this ointment was used to treat scabies. Its potent wound-healing effects were discovered purely by accident.

medicine.name: Herbal Extract
medicine.description: The long-awaited relief from pain is worth any side effects. Herbalists dedicate entire cellars to drying the intoxicating plants used for such blends.

medicine.name: Incense
medicine.description: An aromatic blend of eastern herbs and exotic animal fats, brought to Aldor through the efforts of elven merchants.

medicine.name: Leeches
medicine.description: These vile creatures can be of use if you know how to apply them - and when to pull them off.

medicine.name: Paregoric
medicine.description: A tincture of alcohol, poppy sap, and essential oils, popular among the nobility as a trusted cure for coughs, anxiety, and pain. Many become so addicted to it that they spend days on end in a dreamlike stupor.

medicine.name: Rag
medicine.description: A strip of cloth that can be used to bandage a bleeding wound.

medicine.name: Smoking Mix
medicine.description: A few deep puffs should be enough to settle the nerves and regain lost focus.

medicine.name: Soporific Sponge
medicine.description: The kind of sponge used by city barbers to soothe terrified clients before pulling a bad tooth.

medicine.name: Splint
medicine.description: Handy for setting fractures and securing sprains.

medicine.name: Stardust
medicine.description: A capricious substance of mysterious origin: some partakers complain of dreadful hallucinations, while others claim to glimpse other dimensions... Which, in fairness, sounds like much the same thing.

effects.special: It's best to avoid abusing stardust when your Sanity is low

medicine.name: Surgical Kit
medicine.description: One of those cases where expertise and courage are equally important.

medicine.name: Vivifying Essence
medicine.description: When asked about its recipe, alchemists prefer to maintain a cryptic silence.

elixirs.name: Abasa
elixirs.description: First brewed by a Jibean alchemist from a wormwood blend, abasa took inns and taverns of the realm by storm. Eventually, it was outlawed by the highest decree for its ability to awaken the basest of vices in those who drink it.

elixirs.name: Al'qud
elixirs.description: Maaf warriors often take al'qud before battle to ward off fatigue. Its base is known to be a certain medicinal herb, but the exact way it is prepared remains one of the elves' closely kept secrets.

elixirs.name: Gwynnel's Elixir
elixirs.description: The life's work of Gwynnel, an Aldwynn alchemist. It can wrest even the hopelessly ill from the clutches of death.

elixirs.name: Hornet Honey
elixirs.description: It remains unknown who first thought it would be a good idea to sample deathstinger secretions. Nevertheless, the fact remains: imbibing them briefly sharpens reflexes to an incredible degree. The eventual aftermath comes in the form of a severe headache and full-body cramps.

elixirs.name: Mead
elixirs.description: Northerners can go for weeks without a single crumb of bread, but they start to wither after three days without mead.

elixirs.name: Apple Cider
elixirs.description: Pressed orchard apples left to ferment until the sweetness turns sharp. A Sentian favorite at harvest feasts - it lifts the spirits and loosens the tongue.

elixirs.name: Nikkaf
elixirs.description: Another achievement of elven alchemy. Brynn students in particular are fond of its hunger-numbing and memory-boosting effects - a perfect combination for a night of cramming.

elixirs.name: Night Vision Philter
elixirs.description: A cool blue draught of ginger and berry steeped for dusk watches. Eyes adjust to moonlight; the world sharpens at the edges of shadow.

elixirs.name: Dark Ale
elixirs.description: A mug of good old village ale. In Aldor it is drunk almost as much as water: it fortifies vigor, provides a little nourishment, and helps endure long days in the fields.

elixirs.name: Styptic Brew
elixirs.description: A bitter roadside wash of burnet and nettle. Field surgeons swear by it for closing fresh cuts when bandages run short.

elixirs.name: Clearhead Bitters
elixirs.description: A sharp ginger-and-mindwort draught favored by caravan guards after a night of cheap spirit. It clears the fog, though the taste alone is punishment enough.

elixirs.name: Marching Tea
elixirs.description: A fragrant thyme-and-mint infusion brewed by scouts before long marches. No drunkenness, only a steadier step and clearer head.

elixirs.name: Field Extract
elixirs.description: A crude poppy-and-wormwood soak mixed in camp kettles. Weaker than a proper herbal extract, but still enough to dull a wound when the apothecary is days away.

elixirs.name: Soldier's Draught
elixirs.description: A harsh amber-and-henbane mix issued to levy men before a charge. It puts iron in the arm for a short while, then leaves the tongue bitter and the head swimming.

elixirs.name: Cleaving Bitters
elixirs.description: Honeyed bitters prized by duelists who favor a single decisive cut. Sweet on the first swallow, cruel on the second.

elixirs.name: Bloodwake
elixirs.description: Turquoise-tinted bloodwake is said to thin the foe's armor as much as it thickens one's resolve. Mercenaries drink it before storming plate-clad lines.

elixirs.name: Ironbark Tonic
elixirs.description: Brewed over agate-ground bark powders, ironbark tonic toughens flesh against cuts and bruises. The aftertaste is like chewing wet oak.

elixirs.name: Ward Philter
elixirs.description: A turquoise ward philter whispered over with mindwort prayers. It blunts hostile magic, though some complain of a faint ringing behind the eyes.

elixirs.name: Frostguard
elixirs.description: Amber steeped with lavender against the bite of highland winters and frost-cursed blades. Warmth blooms in the chest, then fades like breath on glass.

elixirs.name: Venomguard
elixirs.description: Azurecap and horsetail rendered into a pale green philter. Hunters sip it before stalking swamp vipers and deathstinger nests.

elixirs.name: Mooncap Elixir
elixirs.description: Moonlit azurecap essence in a clear flask. Weaker than true stardust, yet enough to lend a hedge-mage's cantrips a keener edge.

elixirs.name: Arcane Focus
elixirs.description: Moonstone powder suspended in spirit, steadied with thyme. It gathers a caster's will and quiets the worst misfires - for a price paid in thirst.

elixirs.name: Pyreheart
elixirs.description: Coal-black pyreheart burns going down. It steels the blade-hand and hardens the skin against flame, as if a forge fire briefly took root in the veins.

elixirs.name: Rewoven Philter
elixirs.description: A jewel-tempered spirit said to unstitch the body's hard-won gifts. One draught returns spent attribute points to be allocated anew — at a price few purses survive twice.

elixirs.name: Unlearning Elixir
elixirs.description: Brewed from Gwynnel's work and rare gemstones, this draught unravels trained techniques from muscle and mind. All allocated skill points are refunded — the knowledge remains only as a bitter aftertaste.

spirit.name: Spirit
spirit.description: A base for any potion, sought by alchemists and drunkards alike.

items.name: Flask
items.description: Were it not for the ingenuity of the Bronze Isles' craftsmen, glass bottles might have stayed a luxury forever.

items.name: Bottle of Oil
items.description: It holds a flammable mixture used by wealthy townsfolk to fuel desk lamps.

debuffs.name: Blurred Sight
debuffs.description: Eyes water and edges smear; the world shrinks to a few paces.

debuffs.name: Sticky Feet
debuffs.description: Tar-like residue clings to boots and claws, dragging every step.

debuffs.name: Dazed
debuffs.description: A ringing haze that staggers thought and footing alike.

debuffs.name: Enfeebled
debuffs.description: Limbs feel hollow; blows land soft and aim drifts.

debuffs.name: Terror
debuffs.description: A choking dread that makes hands shake and throats seize.

debuffs.name: Fogged Sight
debuffs.description: A pale mist hangs before the eyes, cutting vision to near nothing.

debuffs.name: Mired
debuffs.description: Heavy sludge around the legs turns a charge into a slog.

debuffs.name: Blinded
debuffs.description: Seared sight leaves only shapes and guesses.

debuffs.name: Rootbound
debuffs.description: Alchemical binders lock joints in place for a few critical turns.

debuffs.name: Crippled
debuffs.description: Joints seize and footing fails; swift killers become easy marks.

throwables.name: Flame Vial
throwables.description: A small flask of lamp oil and powdered charcoal. Shattered against a single foe, it bursts into a brief, clinging flame.

throwables.name: Flame Flask
throwables.description: A heavier spirit-cut fire mixture. On impact it spatters burning oil across a three-by-three pace of ground.

throwables.name: Venom Vial
throwables.description: Puffball toxin sealed in glass. A direct hit soaks one target in virulent poison.

throwables.name: Venom Flask
throwables.description: A volatile spore brew that bursts into a choking poison cloud covering a three-by-three area.

throwables.name: Choke Vial
throwables.description: Hemp smoke and charcoal dust under pressure. Thrown at a single target, it forces a fit of coughing and blurred sight.

throwables.name: Gas Flask
throwables.description: Oil, hemp, and charcoal packed to burst into a spreading haze. The cloud fills a three-by-three space, cutting vision and inviting coughs.

throwables.name: Blur Vial
throwables.description: Mint oil and wormwood soot sealed under pressure. A direct hit smears the enemy's vision into a watery haze.

throwables.name: Tar Vial
throwables.description: Lamp oil thickened with hop resin. It spatters one foe's feet, making every step stick and stumble.

throwables.name: Daze Vial
throwables.description: Ginger heat and henbane vapor packed to burst. The shock leaves a single target reeling and open to missteps.

throwables.name: Weaken Vial
throwables.description: Puffball essence cut with wormwood. Soaked into skin and cloth, it saps the strength behind a foe's swings.

throwables.name: Terror Vial
throwables.description: Henbane and ginger smoke that claws at the nerves. One target coughs, flinches, and fights with shaking hands.

throwables.name: Fog Flask
throwables.description: Oil and smoking mix that blooms into a pale cloud. Across a three-by-three space, eyes water and sight fails.

throwables.name: Mire Flask
throwables.description: Honeyed oil and charcoal grit that splatters into clinging sludge. A three-by-three patch of ground becomes a trap for feet.

throwables.name: Blind Flask
throwables.description: Spirit-cut puffball dust that flares on impact. The cloud sears eyes across a three-by-three area, leaving foes nearly sightless.

throwables.name: Rootbind Flask
throwables.description: A spirit-and-oil binder that hardens on contact. The struck enemy is briefly locked in place, then left heavy-legged.

throwables.name: Cripple Flask
throwables.description: Amber-tempered henbane brew that bursts over a three-by-three space. Joints seize, footwork fails, and counters die in the throat.

coatings.name: Ember Oil
coatings.description: A lamp oil thickened with charcoal and thyme. Rubbed along a blade, it leaves a smoldering sheen that bites with fire on each strike.

coatings.name: Cinder Lacquer
coatings.description: A denser charcoal lacquer laced with henbane. The coated edge glows faintly, as if still resting on the forge.

coatings.name: Venom Lacquer
coatings.description: Death cap and wormwood cooked into oil until the mixture turns sickly green. A thin coat is enough to poison shallow cuts.

coatings.name: Puffball Paste
coatings.description: Pale puffball spores mashed into oil. Assassins favor the paste for its clinging poison that outlasts a brief skirmish.
